Pateman's feminist critique is from a separate, well-documented source (The Sexual Contract, 1988).

ev-poli-regime-types.title: Competitive authoritarianism
ev-poli-regime-types.strength: Tertiary but accurate for this card. The page sets out Levitsky & Way's concept (2002 Journal of Democracy article; 2010 book Competitive Authoritarianism) as a subtype of authoritarianism / hybrid regime: real multiparty elections combined with an unfair playing field, situated against democracy, authoritarianism and totalitarianism. Friedrich & Brzezinski's 1956 six-point totalitarian 'syndrome', Arendt's 1951 Origins of Totalitarianism, and Sartori's 1970 'concept stretching' are well-documented standard attributions verified separately. Whether to use discrete types or a continuous scale is genuinely debated in the field.

ev-poli-democracy.title: Democracy
ev-poli-democracy.strength: Authoritative SEP entry (first published 2006, substantively revised 18 June 2024) covering procedural vs substantive and instrumental vs intrinsic justifications; explicitly discusses Schumpeter's elite/competitive view and Dahl, and foregrounds that the definition itself is contested rather than settling it.

ev-poli-authoritarianism.title: Selectorate theory
ev-poli-authoritarianism.strength: Encyclopaedic summary of the model from Bueno de Mesquita, Smith, Siverson and Morrow's The Logic of Political Survival (2003), including the selectorate/winning-coalition distinction and named criticism by Jessica Weeks on its measurability and behavioural assumptions; an influential but contested formalisation.

ev-poli-democratization.title: Waves of democracy
ev-poli-democratization.strength: Tertiary overview of Huntington's wave thesis (first wave 1828-1926, third from 1974) and reverse waves; the periodisation and the modernization-theory link are named interpretive frameworks (Huntington 1991; Lipset 1959; Przeworski-Limongi 1997), not settled fact.

ev-poli-backsliding.title: Democratic backsliding
ev-poli-backsliding.strength: Canonical overview that names Bermeo's 'executive aggrandizement' and Levitsky & Ziblatt's norms, and cites V-Dem data showing more countries autocratizing than democratizing since c. 2010 (Hungary, Turkey, India, Poland, Brazil, US among cases). The concept and its case list are actively contested, and the article itself flags disagreement over which countries qualify.

ev-poli-separation-powers.title: Separation of powers
ev-poli-separation-powers.strength: Tertiary source; fetch-verified to cover the doctrine from Polybius and Locke through Montesquieu's 1748 'Spirit of the Laws' (including the cited quote) to modern checks-and-balances. The core principle is settled; how strictly to separate versus fuse powers stays a live design debate the article covers.

ev-poli-presidential-parliamentary.title: Presidential system
ev-poli-presidential-parliamentary.strength: Expository overview contrasting presidential and parliamentary forms and presenting Linz's 'perils' critique (rigidity, zero-sum elections) with the named scholarly debate around it; the breakdown claim is a prominent but actively disputed hypothesis (see Cheibub 2007, Mainwaring), not settled consensus.

ev-poli-federalism.title: Federalism
ev-poli-federalism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (first published 2003, substantive revision Nov 2022); covers the division of sovereignty and subsidiarity directly. Expository on a settled concept while flagging real disputes; Riker's 1964 bargaining thesis and Stepan's 1999 'demos-constraining' argument are verified against their original sources, not just the SEP.

ev-poli-veto-players.title: Veto player
ev-poli-veto-players.strength: Tertiary summary of Tsebelis's 2002 book Veto Players: How Political Institutions Work (Princeton UP); accurately states the core stability result and the spatial-model basis, but does not mention Immergut's earlier 'veto points' lineage, which was verified separately against her 1990 Journal of Public Policy article.

ev-poli-bureaucracy.title: Bureaucracy
ev-poli-bureaucracy.strength: Fetch-verified tertiary source: accurately lays out Weber's ideal-type features, rational-legal authority and the 'iron cage', and names Merton's dysfunctions. It does not cover Lipsky's street-level discretion, Niskanen's budget-maximizing model, Dunleavy's bureau-shaping rebuttal or Ferguson's feminist critique — those attributions were verified against the books' own descriptions and the dedicated Wikipedia pages (Budget-maximizing model, Bureau-shaping model).

ev-poli-rule-of-law.title: The Rule of Law
ev-poli-rule-of-law.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry by Jeremy Waldron (first published 2016); authoritative on the formal/procedural vs substantive split, the rule-of-law vs rule-by-law contrast, Fuller's and Raz's formal accounts, and explicit that the thick conception is contested. Thompson's 'unqualified human good' phrase verified to the conclusion of Whigs and Hunters (1975).

ev-poli-ideologies.title: Left–right political spectrum
ev-poli-ideologies.strength: Tertiary overview; fetch-verified to confirm the 1789 National Assembly origin (revolution to the president's left, Ancien Régime to his right) and the 'Criticism' section stating a single axis is too simplistic. Nolan's identity as a libertarian activist and Libertarian Party co-founder verified against the English Wikipedia 'Nolan chart' article.

ev-poli-nationalism.title: Nationalism
ev-poli-nationalism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry that cites Gellner 1983 and Anderson 1983/1991 on the modernity of nations and A. Smith 1986 on ethnic origins, and notes a dissenting deep-roots view (Gat 2013), so it presents the modern-vs-ancient question as contested. It does not cover Chatterjee; that postcolonial critique is verified separately against his The Nation and Its Fragments (1993).

ev-poli-populism.title: Populism
ev-poli-populism.strength: Tertiary survey that states Mudde's 'thin-centred ideology / pure people vs corrupt elite / general will' definition, gives the same left/right examples (Le Pen, Trump; Chavez, Sanders), and lays out the ideational-vs-Laclau/Mouffe (discursive 'logic') dispute even-handedly. Verified live; no dedicated Stanford Encyclopedia entry for 'populism' exists, so Wikipedia is the correct canonical page.

ev-poli-social-movements.title: Social movement
ev-poli-social-movements.strength: Tertiary overview with dedicated sections on resource mobilization (attributed to McCarthy and Zald), political-process/opportunity theory, and Tilly's repertoire of contention (the petition/strike/demonstration/boycott menu, verified against the linked Repertoire of contention and Political opportunity articles). The Melucci/Polletta cultural critique is corroborated by their own work, not the Wikipedia page alone. A maturing-but-contested literature; the cultural critique is acknowledged as a live alternative, not a footnote.

ev-poli-revolution.title: States and Social Revolutions
ev-poli-revolution.strength: Expository page on Skocpol's 1979 book; confirms the state-breakdown-plus-peasant-revolt mechanism and the France/Russia/China cases, and records named critiques of her demotion of agency and ideology, so the contestation is on the record. Davies' 1962 J-curve, Gurr's 1970 'Why Men Rebel', the Phillips quotation, Sewell's ideology critique and Kuran's cascade account were cross-checked against their own canonical pages.

ev-poli-clientelism.title: Clientelism
ev-poli-clientelism.strength: Tertiary entry that defines clientelism through the dyadic, contingent, hierarchical and iterated exchange of goods for support via patron-broker-client ties, sets the explicit contrast with formalised programmatic distribution, and notes the secret-ballot monitoring problem central to Stokes's work; a well-theorised comparative-politics concept.

ev-poli-political-culture.title: The Civic Culture
ev-poli-political-culture.strength: Expository page on Almond & Verba's 1963 book and its parochial/subject/participant typology, the foundation the Putnam social-capital literature builds on; a foundational but heavily critiqued framework, and the Tarrow, Pateman and feminist critiques are named and sourced separately.

ev-poli-civil-society.title: Civil society
ev-poli-civil-society.strength: Tertiary entry placing civil society as the 'third sector' between state and family and covering Tocqueville's associations, Habermas's public sphere, and Gramsci's hegemony reading. The Stanford Encyclopedia has no standalone 'civil society' entry (it appears within the Hegel and Habermas entries), so Wikipedia is the right canonical page for this exact topic; the concept is long-contested, with Gramscian, 'dark side' (Berman) and postcolonial (Chatterjee) readings present in the literature.

ev-epi-what-knowledge.who: SEP (Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup)
ev-epi-what-knowledge.title: The Analysis of Knowledge
ev-epi-what-knowledge.strength: Authoritative SEP entry (substantive revision Jan 2026) that lays out the tripartite JTB analysis, attributes the refuting counterexamples to Gettier (1963), covers Williamson's knowledge-first dissent, and states plainly that no analysis of knowledge has been widely accepted — confirming this is a contested research area, not a settled definition. The named Nyaya/Gangesa comparison is corroborated by SEP's 'Epistemology in Classical Indian Philosophy' (rev. 2024).

ev-epi-gettier.who: SEP (Jonathan Jenkins Ichikawa and Matthias Steup)
ev-epi-gettier.title: The Analysis of Knowledge
ev-epi-gettier.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry that quotes Gettier's 1963 Case I (Smith, Jones and the ten coins) and surveys the proposed fixes (no-false-lemmas, safety, sensitivity, virtue accounts). Honest about contestation: it states plainly that 'no analysis has been widely accepted', and notes some epistemologists now reject analysing knowledge at all.

ev-epi-reliabilism.title: Reliabilist Epistemology
ev-epi-reliabilism.strength: Stanford Encyclopedia entry (first published 2008, substantive revision 2021) co-authored by Goldman, the view's originator — so it is expository but partisan toward reliabilism; it does lay out the generality problem (attributing it to Feldman 1985 and Conee & Feldman 1998) and BonJour's clairvoyant objection, and frames reliabilism as the 'paradigm of externalism' against evidentialism as the 'paradigm of internalism'.

ev-epi-skepticism.who: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy (Juan Comesaña; orig. Peter Klein)
ev-epi-skepticism.title: Skepticism
ev-epi-skepticism.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (first published 2001, substantive revision Jan 2026) covering Cartesian, Pyrrhonian and closure-based skepticism. Even-handed: it lays out the skeptical argument's force and the leading anti-skeptical replies (closure-denial, contextualism, Moorean reversal) rather than declaring a winner. For Putnam's brain-in-a-vat self-refutation, the dedicated SEP entry is at /entries/brain-vat/.

ev-epi-rationalism-empiricism.title: Rationalism vs. Empiricism
ev-epi-rationalism-empiricism.strength: Fetch-verified canonical SEP entry (first published 2004, substantive revision 2 Sep 2021). It frames the debate via the intuition/deduction, innate-knowledge and innate-concept theses, and explicitly cautions that the rationalist/empiricist labelling oversimplifies — noting that almost no thinker falls cleanly into one camp and that figures such as Hobbes, Berkeley, Conway, du Chatelet and Shepherd resist the grouping. So it treats the dichotomy as a useful frame, not a settled taxonomy.

ev-epi-a-priori.title: The Analytic/Synthetic Distinction (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-a-priori.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP survey (substantive revision June 2026) covering Kant's synthetic a priori (§1.1) and Quine's 'Two Dogmas' and confirmation holism (§3.4) in depth; the entry is explicit that whether a viable analytic/synthetic distinction survives Quine's attack remains genuinely contested, so it maps an open debate rather than delivering a verdict.

ev-epi-problem-induction.title: The Problem of Induction (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-problem-induction.strength: Authoritative SEP survey (first published 2018, substantive revision 2022) reconstructing Hume's two-horned dilemma — demonstrative reasoning can't prove the Uniformity Principle, probable reasoning is circular — and surveying the major responses (Bayesian, Strawsonian dissolution, Reichenbach's pragmatic vindication, the material theory). Hume's negative argument is widely regarded as sound; what remains contested is which 'solution' or dissolution to accept, which the entry presents even-handedly.

ev-epi-truth.title: Truth (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-truth.strength: Fetch-verified canonical SEP entry by Michael Glanzberg (substantive revision Jun 27, 2025). Maps correspondence (§1.1, naming Aristotle, Moore, Russell c.1910), coherence (§1.2, exemplified by Joachim 1906 and Blanshard 1939), pragmatist (§1.3, Peirce and James) and deflationary/redundancy theories incl. Ramsey and Horwich's minimalism (§5). A genuinely live dispute with no consensus winner; the entry surveys competing camps and their objections rather than endorsing one.

ev-epi-bayesian.who: Hanti Lin (SEP; rewriting William Talbott's original entry)
ev-epi-bayesian.title: Bayesian Epistemology (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-bayesian.strength: Current SEP entry, first published 2001 by Talbott, completely rewritten by Lin in 2022 and revised 2024. Fetch-verified to cover credences, probabilism, conditionalization, Bayes' theorem, Dutch-book arguments (attributing them to Ramsey 1926 and de Finetti 1937), the probability axioms, the problem of the priors (naming subjective Bayesians de Finetti/Savage vs objective Bayesians Jeffreys/Jaynes), and the problem of old evidence (Glymour 1980, Mercury case). Candid that Bayesianism's foundational arguments are themselves contested.

ev-epi-testimony.title: Epistemological Problems of Testimony (Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-testimony.strength: Peer-reviewed SEP entry (completely rewritten version first published Apr 1, 2021, by Nick Leonard; last substantively revised Feb 16, 2023; the original entry was by Jonathan Adler). Traces reductionism to Hume and non-reductionism to Reid, and surveys Coady's circularity objection, Fricker's local reductionism, and Moran's assurance view. Expository on a question that remains actively disputed; presents the camps even-handedly.

ev-epi-fallibilism.title: Fallibilism (Internet Encyclopedia of Philosophy)
ev-epi-fallibilism.strength: Dedicated, authored encyclopedia entry by epistemologist Stephen Hetherington. Confirms Peirce coined the term, names Descartes' Evil Genius as the foundationalist target, states the 'Fallible Knowledge Thesis' (knowledge from less-than-infallible justification), and discusses the 'self-doubting knowledge claim' that underlies the concessive-knowledge puzzle. Chosen over Wikipedia because it is authored and covers the philosophical detail; chosen because the Stanford Encyclopedia has no dedicated 'fallibilism' slug (the topic is handled inside its contextualism entry). The specific Rysiew/Lewis attributions in the counter are verified against Rysiew's 'Fallibilism, Epistemic Possibility, and Concessive Knowledge Attributions', not this page.

ev-epi-occam.title: Simplicity
ev-epi-occam.strength: Peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry (first published 2004, substantively revised 16 May 2022). Verified to treat Occam's razor as a tie-breaker among theories that 'explain the same set of facts equally well'; to distinguish epistemic vs methodological readings; to flag the entities-vs-equations trade-off ('reducing the ontology... only possible at the price of making it syntactically more complex'); and to source the named positions used here — Popper (simpler = more falsifiable), Swinburne 1997 ('ultimate a priori epistemic principle that simplicity is evidence for truth'), and Sober (parsimony 'always depend[s] on local background assumptions for [its] rational justification'). Ockham's own wording, the John Punch 1639 origin of the Latin slogan, and the precursors (Aristotle, Ptolemy, Duns Scotus) cross-checked against the English Wikipedia 'Occam's razor' article.

ev-epi-scientific-realism.title: Scientific Realism
ev-epi-scientific-realism.strength: Authoritative peer-reviewed expository entry on a genuinely contested debate. Fetch-verified to attribute the no-miracles argument to Putnam (1975, realism 'the only philosophy that doesn't make the success of science a miracle'), the pessimistic meta-induction to Laudan (1981, successful theories 'later rejected'), and to define van Fraassen's constructive empiricism via 'empirical adequacy' (1980). It lays out the live camps even-handedly rather than settling the question.

ev-epi-kuhn.title: Thomas Kuhn
ev-epi-kuhn.strength: Peer-reviewed scholarly entry by a leading Kuhn specialist (first published 2004, substantive revision 2 Sep 2025); fetch-verified to cover normal science as puzzle-solving, paradigms, crisis, revolutions, the three kinds of incommensurability (methodological, perceptual, semantic), and Kuhn's view set explicitly against Popper's falsificationism. Expository on a still-debated thesis (incommensurability remains contested). The counter's 'mob psychology' line is Lakatos's own phrase from his 1970 essay 'Falsification and the Methodology of Scientific Research Programmes', not from this SEP entry.

ev-epi-underdetermination.title: Underdetermination of Scientific Theory
ev-epi-underdetermination.strength: Authoritative scholarly entry (first published 2009, substantive revision 4 Apr 2023; fetch-verified). Develops confirmational (Duhem-Quine) holism, distinguishes it explicitly from contrastive underdetermination, and notes Duhem and Quine ran the two problems together; also covers the Laudan-Leplin (1991) reply. Expository on a debate where the strength of the threat is itself contested.

ev-epi-standpoint.title: Feminist Social Epistemology
ev-epi-standpoint.strength: Peer-reviewed scholarly entry; fetch-verified to cover Hartsock's Marxist-derived standpoint theory, Harding's 'strong objectivity' (examining the world from underprivileged positions), Haraway's 'situated knowledges', the epistemic-advantage thesis, the standpoint-as-'achieved stance' point, and named critics raising the relativism/internalized-oppression worries (Bar On 1993, Walby 2001, Nelson 1990). Longino's critical contextual empiricism and Haack's objectivity critique are documented in the linked SEP entries on feminist epistemology and feminist perspectives on science. Expository on a contested research programme; relativism objections are live.

ev-epi-justification.title: Foundationalist Theories of Epistemic Justification
ev-epi-justification.strength: Authoritative peer-reviewed encyclopedia entry on the regress problem and the foundationalism/coherentism response. The reliabilist alternative the card names is a distinct, well-established externalist position.
